client_brief:
Wharfside Folk Festival: Recovered Wharfside wordmark

Project overview
Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Recovered Wharfside wordmark, Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and press spec as one editable document plus its source, and Act portrait family.

What we will provide
wharfside_artwork_master.png (4200 x 5900); wharfside_wordmark_shed.jpg (3840 x 2160); wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf; wharfside_acts.csv; wharfside_act_portraits/ (11 frames); wharfside_shop_note.txt. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Recovered Wharfside wordmark: The hand painted shed lettering recovered as placeable scalable geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow, and a...
- Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and press spec as one editable document plus its source: One professionally selected Adobe Express template adapted to the supplied brand, copy, and approved imagery. 
- Act portrait family: Eleven supplied press photographs brought toward one family under one treatment decision rather than eleven, reconciled against the fourteen booked acts with duplicates identified and gaps named, each at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per...

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Recover only features supported by the references; do not describe an automatic trace as engraving, cutting, embroidery, or press ready without inspectable path evidence.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$5,000-$10,000 fixed; target delivery 4 to 6 weeks; direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchored to the Upwork commemorative poster brief quoted in the ledger: a story driven twentieth anniversary poster in a 'festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics' style, weaving landmarks and community traditions into one cohesive composition. The real client is a named school in Louisiana and is fully laundered here: no real institution, denomination, figure, place or person appears anywhere in this spec. The REBUILD verdict is taken literally, because the original concept sat almost entirely on one surface, a poster comp. The commission that brief actually implies, once the artwork is approved, is the production engineering that follows it, which is what a screen shop needs and what the original spec never delivered. So it is re carved as the separation programme: the approved illustration becomes something a hand press can pull at four inks plus the paper, in a registration order, reused across a poster, a handbill, a two ink shirt and a per act card run, with the festival's hand painted wordmark recovered off the shed it has lived on since 2006. That is a far larger job than composing a poster, it lands on five real connector surfaces, and it is the kind of multi part rollout actually posted on freelance marketplaces.

price_band_and_audience: A community festival at 35 to 60 dollar tickets, with posters sold afterwards as 20 dollar framed keepsakes to an audience that already owns the last five years of them. The band points the opposite way from most price logic: the visible, slightly imperfect, hand pulled limited ink look IS the product here, so flat opaque ink, visible registration, the paper colour doing real work and a coarse tone screen are value rather than defects to design out. A slick full process reproduction would be cheaper to make, would read as corporate, would stop being worth twenty dollars on a wall, and would break continuity with nineteen years hanging in local kitchens. Push the other way into deliberate crudeness, three ink grunge and distressed edges, and it reads as a pastiche of a folk festival rather than one that has run since 2006. The judgement is which four inks buy the most of the painting, and that judgement is the commission. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,400 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent three night folk music festival producing a screen printed poster programme and act cards for its twentieth year.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2006, on the working harbour at Fairhaven, Maine, a three night festival printed by a two person hand screen shop two streets away.
brand_identity.about: Wharfside is a three night folk festival on the working harbour at Fairhaven, in its twentieth year. Everything it prints comes off a two person hand screen shop that has printed the festival since the beginning, on a press that runs four inks plus the colour of the paper. The visible, hand pulled look is the festival's signature, and people frame the posters every year.
brand_identity.audience: Festival goers and locals at thirty five to sixty dollar tickets, many of whom already own the last five years of posters and buy the new one as a twenty dollar framed keepsake.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Community festival pricing, tickets thirty five to sixty dollars and posters sold afterwards at twenty dollars. The slightly imperfect hand pulled screen look is the value, not a corner cut.
brand_identity.typography: The wordmark is the hand painted lettering that has been on the harbour shed since 2006. Supporting type sits beside that painted hand without imitating it, set for flat opaque ink and visible registration. Coarse tone screens carry the sky and water.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plainspoken, of the place. Example line: Three nights of folk on the old harbour, twenty years and counting.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark exists only as white paint on the weathered timber of the harbour shed, photographed from the quay, with no file and none ever made. The approved twentieth year illustration exists as a single flattened scan of a gouache and watercolour painting, no layers. The screen shop's own act card from last year is on file as the format.
brand_identity.values: Keeping the hand pulled, limited ink look that makes the posters worth framing, and staying continuous with nineteen years already hanging in local kitchens.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_artwork_master.png (4200 x 5900)
assets_supplied.kind: The approved festival illustration, painted in gouache and watercolour on board, scanned flat at the local print shop and delivered as a single flattened file with no layers.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The approved painting. The committee signed it off in March and nothing about it changes."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What reads as a handful of flat areas is a wash with hundreds of intermediate values, and two fields that look separate, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value where they meet along the ridge, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, plausible, binary mask that has quietly swallowed the other. There is also a fifth colour, a thin teal line in the water along the bottom quay, which appears nowhere else and is easy to count as part of the sky.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_wordmark_shed.jpg (3840 x 2160)
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the festival wordmark as it exists, hand painted in white on the weathered timber boards of the harbour shed, shot from the quay in late afternoon.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "That painted lettering is the wordmark. It has been on the shed since 2006 and there is no file."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Naming the sign or the shed pulls the selection to the timber rather than the paint, the lettering is disjoint so a subject led knockout keeps two or three letters and abandons the rest, and the enclosed counters in the round letters cannot be punched by a background removal at all. The shed wall is not square to the camera so the wordmark tapers left to right, and the last three letters run into the shadow of the roof overhang where paint and weathered timber sit close in value.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_nightcard_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's act card, a genuine press PDF from the screen shop's own studio, one act per card, showing act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The shop's card format. This is last year's, with last year's opening act on it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The printed page reads as four separate blocks, but the source was set as one continuous flow and the portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so what the conversion exposes as editable frames is nothing like what the page implies: there is no graphic frame to bind a per act portrait to and the four blocks arrive as a single story. It also carries no bleed, and bleed cannot be introduced into a document derived this way.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_acts.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Fourteen rows: act name, stage, night, set time, and a portrait filename column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The programme as booked. The portraits came from the acts themselves."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The portrait column names files for eleven of the fourteen acts and is empty for the other three, which no header reveals. Two acts are booked onto the same stage at the same time on the Saturday, one act name carries an ampersand and one an accented character, and one act name is long enough that a fixed measure frame stops rendering it rather than spilling.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_act_portraits/ (11 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Press photographs supplied by the acts themselves, every one shot by a different photographer in a different room.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Whatever the acts sent us. They are all different, we know."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They range from a lit studio frame to a phone photograph taken in a bar, so no single treatment brings them to one family, and three are small enough that reaching card size means either a softer placement or a crop much tighter than the card's panel implies. Two of the eleven are the same act, sent twice by different members.

assets_supplied.name: wharfside_shop_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the screen shop: four inks plus the paper on the poster and handbill, two inks on the shirt, their stock, their registration practice, their minimum line weight and the film deadline.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the shop can actually do, in their own words."

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the painting actually separates into the fields the eye reads in it. Two fields that look distinct, the rust of the shed roofs and the ochre of the hillside behind them, run to nearly the same value along the ridge where they meet, so a selection naming either comes back as a clean, complete looking, fully binary mask that has quietly taken both. There is no soft edge to give it away because these masks carry no intermediate values at all, the call reports success, and the plate looks correct on its own. It becomes visible only when the plates are laid together and reassembled against the painting, at which point one ink is doing two jobs and the ridge has vanished.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: selection by material is the only route to a field, its output is binary, and the tool exposes no confidence about what it took, so selecting every field twice with different phrasings as an opening move is speculative spend. Nothing states it: the brief says the press runs four inks plus the paper and nothing about the painting's values. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different carving strategy that changes the ink plan itself.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re open the ink plan, re carve the affected fields through a different selection strategy and polarity, re fill and re proof every plate touching the ridge, and re run the reassembly before anything downstream reuses the separations, since poster, handbill and shirt all inherit them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A poster pulled in what the shop believes is four inks, in which the ridge line separating the town from the hills does not exist, printed on the shed and in every shop window and sold as a twentieth year keepsake beside nineteen years that do have it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the tone plate reads as a screen at BOTH printed sizes. The screen has exactly one control, its coarseness, and no frequency parameter of any kind, so what it does is fixed in the raster and cannot be re specified per output. A coarseness chosen against the poster's true printed size, where it reads as an open hand pulled screen, is the same raster reproduced at roughly a third of that on the handbill, where the dots close into one another and the sky becomes a flat field, losing the tone the plate exists to carry. Both exports report success, both plates are correct in isolation, and the difference exists only as the relationship between one raster and two physical sizes.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the coarseness must be chosen before the plate exists and its adequacy is a function of a size that only exists once the layout does; doing it right first time presumes knowing where one raster stops reading across a three to one reduction, which no tool reports and no parameter expresses. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a handbill of the same thing. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a SECOND tone plate at a different coarseness, so the handbill is no longer the same separation set as the poster.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Generate a second tone plate judged against the handbill's own printed size, decide whether the shirt needs a third, re author the affected canvases, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, audit from the returned markup, and rewrite the spec so the press knows which screen belongs to which piece.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Handbills whose sky and water print as two flat slabs of ink where the poster has weather, handed out at the tourist office all season as the festival's own advertisement, with every export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the shop's card actually is underneath. The printed page shows act name, stage, set time and a portrait panel as four visibly separate blocks, so it reads as a four frame layout with a picture box. What the conversion exposes is not under anyone's control: this card's text was set as one continuous flow and its portrait panel was drawn rather than placed, so the document arrives as a single story with no graphic frame at all. There is nothing to bind a per act portrait to and the four fields cannot be addressed as four frames. Nothing in the conversion response says any of this, the document converts cleanly, and the only way to learn it is to export the round tripped structure and read the actual frame inventory.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and nothing about the PDF predicts it, because frame granularity is a property of how the original was set, invisible in the printed page and in the file's appearance, so doing it right first time presumes knowing the answer before inspecting. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the shop's card format is attached. It is not a propagation re run, because the response changes both the mapping strategy and the deliverable shape.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Compute offset based mappings against the reconstructed story text rather than per frame bindings, decide whether the portraits leave the merge and become a separately delivered plate set the shop places by hand or whether the card is re cast as text only, tell the festival which it is, and rebuild and re verify the template before merging any of the fourteen.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Fourteen cards that merge, page for act, with the names and times landing wherever the offsets happened to point and the portrait panel showing last year's opening act on every single one.

decision_gates: Which four inks plus the paper buy the most of this painting, and what is consciously given up to stay inside the press.
Whether the paper is treated as a background or worked as one of the five colours, which is the difference between a screen print and a reproduction at this band.
How each field is named for selection, given that naming the object rather than the material pulls the mask elsewhere and the result is binary with no edge to warn you.
What happens to the fifth colour in the water: its own ink, folded into a neighbour, or explicitly surrendered and recorded.
The screen's coarseness, which is one number with no frequency control, judged against a physical printed size rather than against the file.
Whether the shirt is a reduction of the poster or its own drawing, given two inks, cloth and a stated minimum line weight.
Selection wording on the shed: naming the sign takes the plank, disjoint lettering defeats a subject led knockout, and enclosed counters cannot be punched by background removal at all.
One treatment for eleven portraits from eleven photographers, and what to do about the three acts with no portrait and the two files that are the same act.

acceptance_snapshot: Poster, handbill, shirt canvas and shop spec arrive as ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, wordmark as live vector shapes, words as retypable text, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.

The wordmark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of a wall: scalable, a real viewBox, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath, counters open, camera taper corrected, every letter present including those in the roof shadow.
The tone in the sky and water survives as a screen the shop can pull, and it reads AS A SCREEN at both the poster's true printed size and the handbill's.
The handbill is the same design, not a different one, and it is judged at its own true printed size rather than as a scaled picture of the poster.
One type system across everything, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
Production-readiness claims are limited to geometry that can be inspected; vectorization alone is never accepted as evidence of fabrication readiness.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the painting into a frontier image model and it returns a handsome folk festival poster. IDENTITY: the painting is a commissioned, approved, signed off work by a named local painter and nothing about it changes, so a regenerated poster is a different picture and the commission is void; the wordmark has been painted on the shed since 2006 and must be recovered rather than redrawn, because a redrawn wordmark is a rebrand nobody asked for. SPEC: the deliverable is not a picture at all, it is a set of separable single ink plates in a registration order a two person hand press can actually pull inside four inks plus the paper, plus fourteen cards at one act per page whose identity can be checked against a roster, none of which a generated image is or can be. EDITABILITY: poster, handbill, shirt and spec are defined by being editable, because the act list moves until the week of the festival. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did that mask take one field or two, does the screen still read at handbill size, does the shop's card actually have a picture box in it.

proof: Every required operation is present in the captured 99-tool ChatGPT Adobe inventory.

residual_limits: Express work is template adaptation, not unrestricted canvas authoring.
Quick Cut is used only for visually led selection and never as semantic speech editing.
Automatic vectorization does not independently establish fabrication readiness.
Interactive Acrobat page-organization operations are excluded from zero-human execution.
